scope: Pinned flat Pike VM and bounded lazy DFA regex engine, native and web. All fourteen regex runtime comparisons pass. Six of twelve compilation comparisons pass; six inconclusive, no established regression. Existing whole-stage uncertainties remain.

correctness.oracle: 121 deterministic Python-re comparisons in each native/web default/release mode, covering ordered alternatives, captures, empty matches, Unicode byte spans, 255/256/257-byte boundaries and a 12000-character DFA-state-limit input. Repeated empty capture conventions are excluded from Python equivalence. Four additional API cases cover replacements, offsets, malformed bytes, pattern errors. Two pinned upstream fixture modes.
correctness.harness_smoke: Maintained benchmark module exercised with iteration divisor 1000. Those samples are correctness-only and are not used for performance acceptance. Its full-sized generated source hashes and independent checksums match the measured prototype exactly.
correctness.measurement_correction: The initial Unicode benchmark expected byte lengths for Match.text; Dewy len returns grapheme length. Corrected the independent expectation before collecting Unicode samples. Previously completed ASCII workloads were retained without resampling.

runtime.clock: thread CPU nanoseconds, matching and result allocation included; input and Regex construction outside timer except short-prepare

limits: Native 64-bit host. Warm filesystem caches; one build per binary.
C graph uses flat edges and a handwritten map; Dewy uses per-node arrays and an insertion-ordered map.
String equality uses separately allocated payloads; C uses pointer/length pairs and libc memcmp, Dewy uses runtime strings.
Kernel times exclude input generation; wall times include the complete process.
Thread CPU timing excludes descheduling, but CPU frequency and cache contention still matter.
